updates.title: AWS adds Smart Approvals to Amazon Quick
updates.whatChanged: AWS added Smart Approvals to Amazon Quick on 4 November. A classifier reviews actions marked Ask each time against the request and conversation. It auto-approves low-risk actions and sends consequential actions or review failures to a person. Quick logs activity in CloudTrail. Smart Approvals is on by default in desktop and mobile apps. The web version does not support it.
updates.whyCare: Your Quick agents can finish routine multi-step tasks without repeated approval prompts, while connector policies still reserve consequential actions for a person. The classifier can err, so keep mandatory approvals in policy and audit a pilot.
updates.before: Quick sent actions marked Ask each time to the user for approval. That could interrupt routine steps in multi-action workflows.
updates.after: Quick now reviews eligible actions against the request and context, approves low-risk actions for their exact parameters, and returns consequential actions or review failures to a person.
updates.learn: Pilot Smart Approvals with a defined workflow. Require human review through connector permissions for actions that must never be auto-approved. Audit sample approvals in CloudTrail before expanding access.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning Blog - Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters
Amazon Quick User Guide - Smart Approvals

updates.architectureImplication: Keep authorization in existing connector and account policies, then use the classifier only to decide which eligible actions still need a person. Preserve explicit approval rules for sensitive actions and correlate Quick events with destination-system logs.

action.what: Confirm connector permissions and audit logging before piloting Smart Approvals.
